session.title: Gmail MCP Server — Build Session
session.goal: Build a Gmail MCP server that connects Claude AI to Gmail for reading, sending, and managing emails

phases.title: Project Discovery
phases.summary: Explored the existing gmail-mcp project structure. Found that the core files (index.js, gmail.js, auth.js) were already written but dependencies were not installed and credentials were missing.

phases.title: Google OAuth Setup
phases.summary: User created a Google Cloud project, enabled Gmail API, set up OAuth consent screen, and created a Desktop OAuth client. Created credentials.json template for the user to fill in.
steps_completed: User filled in client_id and client_secret
Removed gmail.metadata scope (was conflicting with gmail.readonly)
Deleted old token.json and re-ran auth

issues_faced.error: Metadata scope doesn't allow format FULL
issues_faced.fix: Removed gmail.metadata from SCOPES in auth.js
Killed process using lsof -ti:3141 | xargs kill -9

phases.title: Connect to Claude Desktop
phases.summary: Registered the MCP server with Claude Desktop by adding mcpServers config to claude_desktop_config.json. Server started working after restart.

phases.title: Testing Gmail Tools
phases.summary: Successfully fetched last 5 emails and searched for job-related emails directly from Claude Code session using the Gmail API.

tests_run.email_found: Groww is hiring interns! — from Unstop via Unstop newsletter

phases.title: Credential Path Migration
phases.summary: Moved credentials from project folder to ~/.gmail-mcp/ so the server works correctly when installed globally via npm.
changes: Changed TOKEN_PATH and CREDS_PATH to use os.homedir() + '.gmail-mcp/'

phases.title: npm Publishing Attempt
phases.summary: Attempted to publish the package to npm as @suryansh0910/gmail-mcp. Failed due to 2FA being enabled on the npm account without an authenticator app available.
changes_made: Updated package.json with proper metadata (keywords, author, license)
Added gmail-mcp and gmail-mcp-auth as bin entries
Changed package name to @suryansh0910/gmail-mcp (gmail-mcp was already taken at v2.3.1)
Made bin files executable with chmod +x

issues_faced.fix: Not resolved — no authenticator app available. To be done later.

phases.title: GitHub Repository Setup
phases.summary: Decided to publish on GitHub instead of npm. Set up .env-based credentials so client_id and client_secret are not exposed in the repo.
changes_made: Created .env file with GMAIL_CLIENT_ID and GMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET
Created .env.example as a template for users
Updated auth.js and gmail.js to read from process.env instead of credentials.json
Reverted package name back to gmail-mcp
git_commands: git commit -m 'Initial commit: Gmail MCP server for Claude'

phases.title: HTTP Server for claude.ai Web
phases.summary: Built an HTTP-based MCP server (src/http.js) so the service works on claude.ai web (not just Claude Desktop). Used ngrok to expose it publicly.

issues_faced.error: Not Acceptable: Client must accept text/event-stream
issues_faced.fix: Switched from StreamableHTTP to SSE transport
Passed req.body explicitly to transport.handlePostMessage(req, res, req.body)

phases.title: Multi-user OAuth Flow
phases.summary: Extended http.js to support multiple users — each user authenticates their own Gmail instead of everyone sharing the developer's Gmail.
flow_implemented: GET / → Landing page with 'Connect your Gmail' button
GET /auth → Generates userToken, redirects to Google OAuth
GET /auth/callback → Exchanges code for tokens, stores in memory Map
Each MCP request looks up user's token and builds their own auth client

issues_faced.cause: Google OAuth app in Testing mode — only whitelisted emails can log in
issues_faced.fix: Add user email manually in Google Cloud Console → OAuth consent screen → Test users

issues_faced.cause: Desktop OAuth client doesn't support custom redirect URIs
issues_faced.fix: Created a new Web application OAuth client with ngrok callback URL registered

issues_faced.cause: ngrok forwards as http internally, BASE_URL was set to http://

http_server.auth: Multi-user — each user authenticates their own Gmail via /auth

technologies_used.name: ngrok
technologies_used.purpose: Exposes local server to public internet

technologies_used.name: sharp
technologies_used.purpose: Auto-compress oversized images before attaching to emails

additional_phases.title: MCP OAuth Protocol Implementation
additional_phases.summary: Founder feedback: flow was too complicated. Rebuilt http.js to implement the MCP OAuth protocol so claude.ai handles the login journey natively. User just adds the URL to claude.ai connector and clicks 'Login with Google' — no token copying or landing pages.
additional_phases.founder_feedback: Too complicated. Put URL in claude.ai → claude.ai takes you on login journey → user does ok/login → end of flow → Gmail works in Claude
endpoints_added: GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server — OAuth discovery metadata for claude.ai
GET /authorize — Redirects user to Google OAuth
GET /callback — Exchanges Google code for Gmail tokens, redirects back to claude.ai
POST /token — claude.ai exchanges auth code for Bearer token
additional_phases.how_it_works: claude.ai reads the OAuth discovery endpoint, triggers the Google login flow automatically, stores the Bearer token, and includes it in all future MCP requests. Server looks up the token to find the user's Gmail credentials.

additional_phases.title: Credential Split — Desktop vs Web OAuth Client
additional_phases.summary: Separated credentials into two OAuth clients: Desktop client for local auth (auth.js / Claude Desktop) and Web application client for HTTP server (http.js / claude.ai web). This was needed because Web application clients require custom redirect URIs and Desktop clients work better with localhost.

env_structure.GMAIL_CLIENT_ID: Desktop OAuth client — used by auth.js and index.js
env_structure.WEB_CLIENT_ID: Web application OAuth client — used by http.js
env_structure.BASE_URL: Public ngrok URL for the HTTP server

issues_faced.issue: Web application client failing with localhost auth
issues_faced.error: Something went wrong — Google OAuth error on localhost
issues_faced.fix: Used Desktop client for local auth, Web client only for HTTP server

additional_phases.title: Attachment Support — Images and PDFs
additional_phases.summary: Added file attachment support to send_email tool. Also added send_email_with_url_attachment tool so users can attach files by providing a URL (server downloads directly). Added auto-compression for large images using sharp.
tools_added: send_email — updated with attachments[] parameter (filename, mimeType, base64 data)
send_email_with_url_attachment — new tool, server fetches file from URL directly

issues_faced.cause: Claude times out trying to pass large base64 images through MCP tool calls
issues_faced.fix: Added sharp auto-compression (resize to 1200px, 75% JPEG quality) for images over 1MB
Added send_email_with_url_attachment tool — server downloads file from URL, bypassing Claude's payload limit entirely

key_decisions.decision: Use stdio transport for Claude Desktop
key_decisions.reason: Simplest approach — no hosting needed, Claude Desktop spawns the process directly
Keeps OAuth credentials out of the public GitHub repo

key_decisions.decision: Store tokens in ~/.gmail-mcp/ instead of project folder
key_decisions.reason: Works correctly when installed globally via npm or npx

key_decisions.decision: Per-user token via URL query param (?token=xxx)
key_decisions.reason: Simple stateless approach — no cookies or sessions needed, works with claude.ai's integration system
npm publish blocked by 2FA. GitHub lets anyone clone and run immediately.
